headline: Toledo's $20M RAISE grant confirmed — 38-block Junction/Uptown/Englewood reconstruction advances to construction prep
paragraphs: The federally-funded $53M project covering 38 blocks (13th–21st Street, Adams to Monroe) is in design through 2026, construction 2027–2029, completion targeted 2031. Funded by a $20M USDOT RAISE grant.

The Blade reported August 25, 2026 that Toledo has received formal confirmation of its $20 million U.S. Department of Transportation RAISE grant for the Connecting Toledo Neighborhoods to Opportunity initiative. The award covers 38 city blocks in the Junction, Uptown, and Englewood neighborhoods, funding new water and sanitary utilities, road reconstruction and resurfacing, pedestrian and bicycle facilities, and streetscapes. The confirmation comes as the project's design phase wraps up ahead of a planned 2027 construction start; the total project budget is $52.9 million.
why_it_matters: Biggest neighborhood-scale infrastructure investment in this part of Toledo in a generation. Junction's 45% vacancy rate means infrastructure is going in ahead of private development — a deliberate "build it and they will come" bet.
